title: He opened the vault…
paragraphs:
He opened the vault…
and exposed his heart.
And that moment… almost rewrote his legacy.

Because what looked like success…
was actually surrender to pride.
The kind that smiles while it destroys you.
King Hezekiah had just experienced a miracle.

Death was at his door—
and God pushed it back.

Fifteen more years of life (Isaiah 38:5).
Healing in his body.
Deliverance in his nation.

Why would a man who just witnessed God’s power
suddenly feel the need to prove his own?

Sometimes it whispers:
“Let them see what you have now.”

“Let them admire what God gave you…
without mentioning God.”
Hezekiah failed a test he didn’t even know he was taking.
Scripture cuts straight through the illusion:

“However, regarding the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon…
God left him alone, to test him, that He might know all that was in his heart.”
— 2 Chronicles 32:31

Not to abandon him.
But to reveal him.

And what came out…
was pride.

“But Hezekiah did not repay according to the favor shown him,
for his heart was lifted up…”
— 2 Chronicles 32:25
And here is the consequence most people miss:

“Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house…
shall be carried to Babylon. Nothing shall be left.”
— Isaiah 39:6

The very thing you flaunt
can become the very thing you lose.
This is not just ancient history.

We do it with achievements.
With platforms.
With relationships.
With blessings.

And slowly… subtly…
the center shifts.
But here’s where the Gospel crashes in with holy mercy.
Because where Hezekiah exposed his treasures…
Yet He didn’t open heaven to impress us.
He came down to save us.
He didn’t say, “Look at My riches.”
He said, “I will become your redemption.”
And here’s the truth we cannot ignore:
Pride is not just a personality flaw.

It replaces dependence on God
with confidence in self.

It robs God of glory
and hands it to dust.

“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
— James 4:6
But don’t miss the second half.

To the one who says,
“Lord… this isn’t mine. It’s Yours.”

To the one who stops performing
and starts surrendering.

Because you’ve been posting victories
but hiding your dependence on God.

Maybe you’ve been building an image
instead of cultivating intimacy.

Maybe you’ve been showing people your treasures…
but not showing God your heart.
God is not after your gold.
Because the danger is not in having blessings.
The danger is in believing they came from you.
Hezekiah’s story is not just a warning.
An invitation to come back down.
“God, everything I have… is because of You.”
And if pride has already crept in?
Because Jesus didn’t just die for obvious sins.
He died for hidden pride too.

At the cross, pride is exposed…
and forgiven.

At the cross, self is crucified…
and new life begins.
You don’t have to keep performing.
You don’t have to protect your image.
You don’t have to prove anything.

What am I showing off
that I should be surrendering?

What am I taking credit for
that belongs to God?

What would my life look like
if Jesus—not my success—was the headline?
Say it if you mean it:

“Jesus, humble my heart.
Be my treasure.”
If this stirred something in you…
